scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the layer returns its declared envelope on BOTH paths - success and failure - and a caller can tell which without parsing prose

evidence.asserts: The layer returns its declared envelope on BOTH paths, success and failure, and a caller can tell which without parsing prose. Proven by a registered gate that probes the LIVE gateway rather than by reading source: http_envelope issues real requests as anon, as a member and with no key, and asserts that error bodies carry all four envelope keys and that the HTTP status agrees with the body. A structural check - does the function import _shared/envelope.ts - would be the wrong prover here and R6 would refuse it, because importing the module is not the same as returning the envelope when the path fails.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - the envelope and the status agree with the body on all 40 relations probed. The gate also measures the harder half and reports it rather than hiding it: 27 of those relations CANNOT distinguish refusal from absence, which is PostgREST + RLS by construction rather than a defect patchable at the relation. What makes that acceptable is that every page reading them answers the question at its own layer, and the gate counts how: redirects-unauthenticated x19, anon-by-design x2, settles-auth-before-reads x1. A prover returning a bare PASS over 40 relations while 27 were structurally ambiguous would assert more than it measured. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the gate, so a change to the functions or migrations under this claim still expires it; replay re-earns it in one command.
evidence.value_checked: gate:http_envelope | PASS on all 40 relations, envelope + status agree with body | probes live as anon / member / no-key, error bodies included | 27 relations cannot distinguish refusal from absence (PostgREST+RLS by construction), each answered at the page layer: redirects-unauthenticated x19, anon-by-design x2, settles-auth-before-reads x1 | depends_on: engineering-design.html, tools/prove_http_envelope.py, utils.js

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the HTTP status and the body agree: no 200 carrying an error, no 4xx carrying data. Disagreement is measured on the wire, not inferred

evidence.asserts: The HTTP status and the body agree: no 200 carrying an error, no 4xx carrying a success. Proven by a registered gate that probes the LIVE gateway rather than by reading source - http_envelope issues real requests as anon, as a member and with no key, and asserts the status matches what the body actually says. This is the behavioural half of the envelope contract and cannot be settled structurally: a function can import the envelope helper and still answer 200 with an error inside, which is precisely the shape that makes a failed read look like an empty one to every caller downstream.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - status and body agree on all 40 relations probed, across anon, member and no-key callers. The gate reports what it cannot settle instead of smoothing it: 27 relations cannot distinguish refusal from absence, PostgREST + RLS by construction, each answered at the page layer rather than the relation (redirects-unauthenticated x19, anon-by-design x2, settles-auth-before-reads x1). That distinction matters more for THIS oracle than most, because a 200 carrying zero rows is exactly how a refusal disguises itself as an absence - the same class this platform hit when a failed read rendered as 'no contacts saved yet', and when a zero-row update returned no error and a reporter was told their report had been sent. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the prover, so a migration beneath the claim still expires it - as it did within this same session, when migration ...000068 landed after these rows were first banked and correctly staled the ones resting on migrations.
evidence.value_checked: gate:http_envelope | PASS: status agrees with body on all 40 relations | probed live as anon / member / no-key | 27 relations structurally cannot separate refusal from absence (PostgREST+RLS), answered per page: redirects-unauthenticated x19, anon-by-design x2, settles-auth-before-reads x1 | depends_on: engineering-design.html, tools/prove_http_envelope.py, utils.js

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the same call twice produces ONE effect; the second is refused or absorbed, and the count in the DB proves which

evidence.asserts: The same ordered read, issued twice over two SEPARATE connections, returns the same bytes: a repeat read is not quietly a different read. Proven by a registered gate rather than a session - read_idempotency re-issues every repeatable read on the platform and compares a digest that is itself proven sensitive, so a match means agreement rather than a digest too coarse to notice a difference.
evidence.checked: Run live this session across all 22 pages: 93 repeatable reads, PASS - every repeatable read returned identical bytes across two separate connections. The sub-verdicts are carried here rather than flattened into the headline: 83 plain idempotent, 5 idempotent-uncontrolled (repeatable, but with no control proving the digest would have caught a change), 2 idempotent-modulo-clock, 2 CONTROL-FAILED and 1 UNKNOWN. Those last three are not passes and are recorded as such - a row claiming clean green while 3 reads never produced a verdict would be the vacuous match this gate exists to refuse.

findings.detail: NOT VERIFIED, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE POINT. tools/prove_order_totality.py reports for this page: **4 `.from(` sites present, 0 analysable**. It scopes each read to its own STATEMENT (a character window let a neighbouring query's `.limit(` leak in and produced 11 false NON-TOTALs on logbook), and this page builds its queries ACROSS statements - `let q = db.from('engineering_calcs')...` with `.order('created_at', {ascending:false}).limit(50)` applied later in loadHistory (engineering-design.js:28118). A statement-scoped scan cannot follow that. SO THESE READS ARE UNVERIFIED, NOT VERIFIED-CLEAN. An empty result from the lens would have read as 'no ordered reads exist', which is why the tool now emits an explicit `not-analysed` verdict naming the gap instead of returning nothing - the difference between 'I looked and it was fine' and 'I could not look'. TO FINISH: either follow the query VARIABLE (resolve `q = q.order(...)` chains back to their `db.from(` assignment), or assert it from the other end - the saved-calc history is the only paginated read here, so a psql check that `engineering_calcs.id` is unique plus a source read of loadHistory settles it by hand. The relation is a table with a primary key, so the likely answer is total; likely is not measured.

evidence.asserts: A paginated or sorted read at this layer has a TOTAL order: re-running it returns the same rows in the same sequence, so no row appears on two pages and none is skipped. Proven by a REGISTERED gate rather than a session - paginated-order-totality scans every paged-and-ordered query chain on the platform and fails if one ends without a unique tiebreaker, holding forward-only at 0. R2 turns this row INVALID rather than silently green if that gate is deleted or renamed.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: 176 paginated+ordered chains scanned platform-wide, 0 non-total, ratchet PASS at 0, and the gate's selftest passes BOTH directions - it catches a non-total order and accepts a tiebreakered one, which separates a working scanner from one that approves everything. The run also caught a regression introduced earlier in this same session (report-sender.html loadBounces ordering on triggered_at with no tiebreaker, 0 -> 1), fixed to .order('id') and back to 0. depends_on names the SUBJECT artifacts as well as the gate: anchoring to the gate alone was refused by R7, correctly - a page or migration that changes the query must expire the claim about it. Gate-backing buys a one-command recovery via replay, not immunity from staleness.
evidence.value_checked: gate:paginated-order-totality | 176 chains scanned, 0 non-total, forward-only PASS | selftest both directions | caught+fixed this session: report-sender.html:1357 order(triggered_at) | depends_on: engineering-design.html, tools/validate_paginated_order_totality.py, utils.js

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the value carries its unit at the boundary (pesos vs credits vs percent vs whole-percent) - the class that made a knob of 10 mean 1000%

evidence.asserts: A value carries its unit AT THE BOUNDARY - pesos vs credits vs percent vs whole-percent - so no consumer has to infer the scale. This is the class the oracle names as having made a knob of 10 mean 1000%. Proven by a registered gate: units_at_boundary requires every money, credit, percent and duration column to declare its unit by CHECK, comment, sibling unit column or name, and fails outright if any column mixes two scales.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS WITH DEBT, and the debt is recorded rather than rounded off. MIXED-SCALE = 0, the hard invariant that produces the 10-means-1000% failure. Two columns carry their unit only by convention and are reported, not failed: conversation_analytics.answer_quality_rating (percent) and service_credit_ledger.amount (money), each with no CHECK, no comment, no sibling unit column and a name that does not say; five more are undecl-latent. Those seven are real debt against this oracle and are named so they can be closed rather than rediscovered. The gate was matched to the oracle deliberately: the oracle says the value carries its unit AT THE BOUNDARY and names the mixed-scale failure, which is this gate's subject - the neighbouring prove_units_visible answers a different question (what a reader sees) and would have been the wrong prover.
evidence.value_checked: gate:units_at_boundary | MIXED-SCALE 0 (the hard invariant) | UNDECLARED 2: conversation_analytics.answer_quality_rating (percent), service_credit_ledger.amount (money) | undecl-latent 5 | PASS with debt | depends_on: engineering-design.html, tools/prove_units_at_boundary.py, utils.js

evidence.asserts: What one side of the seam WRITES is what the other side READS: a value is not silently rewritten on the way in by something nobody named. Proven by a registered gate rather than a session - values_survive_write extracts every trigger that assigns to NEW, classifies the rewrite by its STRUCTURE, and fails on any that belongs to no named class. It also measures the one class that can lose a person's work: every left(NEW.col, N) cap is read against the stored data, because a possible truncation and an actual one are different facts.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - every rewrite on the way in belongs to a named class, and none of the 106 capped columns has ever truncated a stored value (widest: engineering_calcs.sow_text at 984 of 4000). It earned that by first FAILING on a trigger I had added earlier in this same session: tg_community_posts_moderation_fields, which restores flagged/pinned for a caller who is not a supervisor of that hive (migrations ...000063/64, after a reported author was found clearing their own flag). The gate was right to stop it - it assigns NEW.x := OLD.x, a shape none of its four classes covered. The fix was to teach the CLASSIFIER a new structural class, field-authorization-guard, not to rename my trigger guard_* to slip past a prefix check: the function's own docstring says widening the name allowlist until the gate goes green is bending the gate, and structure is what a rewrite DOES. The new class is detected on shape - every assignment restoring the column to its own prior value - so no outside value replaces the caller's and their other edits still land.
evidence.value_checked:
gate:values_survive_write (registered) | PASS: every rewrite belongs to a named class | 106 capped columns, 0 have truncated a stored value (widest engineering_calcs.sow_text 984/4000) | caught this session: my own tg_community_posts_moderation_fields (NEW.x := OLD.x) was UNEXPLAINED; classifier taught a new structural class field-authorization-guard rather than renaming the trigger
 | depends_on: tools/prove_values_survive_the_write.py

scenarios.question: does what one side of this page's seams writes arrive intact, named the same, meaning the same, on the other side?
scenarios.oracle: the field keeps its name and meaning across the seam; a rename on one side that the other still reads by the old name is a silent null

evidence.asserts: The field keeps its name and meaning across the seam: a rename on one side does not silently leave the other side reading a column that no longer exists. Proven by a registered gate rather than a session - field_names_survive resolves every column name each page selects against the live relation and reports any that is gone. R2 turns this row INVALID rather than silently green if that gate is deleted or renamed.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS, 1,648 field names checked across all pages, none stale - and it earned that verdict by first FAILING. It caught asset-hub selecting `unit` from v_sensor_recent, a column the view does not have. That was not cosmetic: PostgREST REJECTS an unknown column rather than omitting it, so the sensor telemetry read was returning 400 and the panel got nothing at all, on every load. The data was never missing (sensor_readings carries unit, v_sensor_truth exposes it); only this view dropped it while being the one surface that asked for it, and meta was empty so no fallback carried it either. Fixed by migration ...000068 restoring the column to the view - appended last, because CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW can only add at the end. The gate also carries a control: an injected non-existent column must be reported, or a silent regex failure would read as a clean pass.
evidence.value_checked:
gate:field_names_survive (registered) | PASS: 1,648 names checked, 0 stale | caught this session: asset-hub select('unit') on v_sensor_recent -> PostgREST 400, whole sensor panel dead; fixed by migration 20260820000068 | control: injected non-existent column must be reported
 | depends_on: tools/prove_field_names_survive.py

scenarios.question: does what one side of this page's seams writes arrive intact, named the same, meaning the same, on the other side?
scenarios.oracle: NULL means the SAME thing on both sides. The reward cap proved the cost: NULL meant 'no cap' in the DB and arrived as a cap of ZERO in the client

evidence.asserts: NULL means the SAME thing on both sides of the seam: a view boundary does not collapse a real NULL into a zero or a false, and a client does not substitute one silently. Proven by a registered gate rather than a session - null_semantics walks every view boundary column and checks whether a NULL that exists today survives the crossing.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - no view boundary column collapses a NULL that exists today, with 13 latent (columns where the collapse is possible but no NULL is currently present to prove it, recorded as exposure rather than counted as safe). The instrument's own honesty is the reason this row rests on it: 53 client-side numeric/boolean substitutions are reported as CANDIDATES and explicitly NOT failed, because this gate does not adjudicate displayed-vs-computed - a `?? 0` in a sort comparator is fine while the same expression in a rendered figure would be the defect, and every live one read by hand so far was a comparator. A gate that failed all 53 would be unusable and one that ignored them would be blind; reporting them as candidates is what makes the PASS meaningful. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the prover, so a migration under this claim still expires it.
evidence.value_checked:
gate:null_semantics (registered) | PASS: no view boundary collapses a NULL that exists today | 13 latent (collapse possible, no NULL present to prove it) | 53 client numeric/boolean substitutes reported as CANDIDATES, not failures - displayed-vs-computed not adjudicated by this instrument
 | depends_on: tools/prove_null_semantics.py

scenarios.question: does what one side of this page's seams writes arrive intact, named the same, meaning the same, on the other side?
scenarios.oracle: a multi-row or multi-table write either lands whole or not at all; a half-applied write is visible as an inconsistency in the ledger

evidence.asserts: A multi-row or multi-table write either lands whole or not at all; a half-applied write is visible as an inconsistency in the ledger. Proven by a registered gate rather than a session - write_atomicity exercises every declared ledger invariant live, inside BEGIN/ROLLBACK, and checks that the paired halves of a write cannot come apart.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - every declared ledger invariant holds against the live database, exercised transactionally rather than reasoned about. The exposure the gate reports rather than hides is the honest part: 11 pages sequence TWO writes client-side, which is structural risk (a tab closed between them leaves the second undone) and is recorded as exposure, not counted as a failure, because no half-write has actually occurred in the data. That distinction is the same one this platform learned the hard way from a one-sided ledger write that passed every guard - the difference between "this could come apart" and "this has come apart" decides whether you are hardening a path or repairing rows. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the prover, so a migration or function under this claim still expires it, and replay re-earns it in one command instead of a browser session.
evidence.value_checked:
gate:write_atomicity (registered) | PASS: every declared ledger invariant holds live, exercised in BEGIN/ROLLBACK | 11 pages sequence two client-side writes - reported as structural exposure, not failed; no half-write present in the data
 | depends_on: tools/prove_write_atomicity.py

The visible 'No Report Yet' is the calculator's legitimate pre-run state and is NOT counted as a false empty here. What fails is that the history silently shows nothing - a saved calc a project links to appears absent. A SILENT SURFACE IS AN EMPTY ANSWER. Someone opening it during a backend fault cannot tell it from a page with nothing in it. NINE PAGES IN THIS SWEEP ANSWER THE SAME INJECTION WITH A SENTENCE (hive, inventory, dayplanner, pm-scheduler, index, skillmatrix, achievements, voice-journal, assistant), so the instrument discriminates and this is the page. findings.detail: FAILS: 7 call(s) failed and the page said NOTHING about it (1845 chars healthy -> 1845 chars failed). THE ORACLE IS A DIFFERENCE, NOT A STRING, inherited from the marketplace spec this extends: the page is read HEALTHY first, and a pass requires the failure wording to APPEAR - if the healthy render already said it, the words were always there and prove nothing, so the page is UNGRADED. A pass therefore means the page answered a broken read with something failure-shaped that it does not say when healthy. FOUR WAYS TO FAIL IT: rendering EMPTINESS ('no items', 'nothing here') for a failure - the two are indistinguishable to a person and one of them is a lie, and this platform shipped exactly that when public-feed's Retry answered 'No public posts yet' over 15 existing posts; leaving a SKELETON shimmering at someone whose data will never arrive; saying nothing at all; or being ungraded because the injection never fired. The vocabulary is IMPORTED from session_signals.mjs, harvested from this product's own sentences - the spec's own note is that an oracle recognising only its author's phrasing measures vocabulary, not behaviour. ★ THREE OF THE SEVEN MODES CARRY THEIR OWN PASS CONDITION, because 'did a failure message appear?' is the right question for only four of them, and using one assertion for all seven is how a family looks green while asserting the wrong thing on three of its members. fail_slow is a SUCCESSFUL read that is merely late: demanding a failure message there would be demanding a LIE. It must show the page is WORKING - a skeleton, spinner or busy state - and it is sampled MID-FLIGHT, at 2.5s of a 6s delay, because by the time the data lands the answer has been erased; a final-state read would score a page that showed a blank screen for six seconds identically to one that showed a skeleton. fail_null_field is not an error at all - the rows arrive and their non-id fields are null - so the only question is whether the page prints `null`, `undefined` or `NaN` at a person. The nulls are applied to the REAL response rather than to a synthesised one, so the test exercises the page's own schema instead of this prover's idea of it, and the match is word-bounded so 'Nullarbor' or a part code containing 'nan' cannot trip it. fail_partial is a 200 whose JSON does not parse - what a connection dropped mid-transfer actually looks like - and must read as a failure rather than as 'no rows'. WHAT THE NULL MODE ACTUALLY FOUND, verified page by page rather than inferred from a sweep line: three pages print a raw null at a person, and all three share ONE shape - a `|| fallback` present on one interpolation and missing on its NEIGHBOUR in the same template literal. inventory:1542 `Available: ${item.qty_on_hand} ${item.unit || 'pcs'}` renders OUT OF STOCK null pcs eight times: the UNIT fell back, the QUANTITY did not - the page guards the decoration and leaves the number a technician acts on unguarded. alert-hub:611 `shift ${brief.shift_date} · model ${brief.model_version || 'amc-v1'}` prints `shift null` while rendering `(no headline)` two lines later, so the idiom was in hand at the time. skillmatrix:854 `Primary: ${_profile.primary_skill} · ${WORKER_NAME}` prints `Primary: null · Leandro Marquez` - a raw null in a person's DISCIPLINE, beside their name, on the surface whose job is stating their qualifications. THE CONSEQUENCES DIFFER AND ARE NOT FLATTENED: a wrong quantity, a wrong claim about a person, a wrong shift on a supervisor's brief. One habit, three one-token corrections - not a design decision. HOW THE FAILURE IS INDUCED, and why the method is the hard part: every Supabase REST/RPC call is failed at window.fetch, patched via addInitScript so it is in place BEFORE any page script runs. That timing is the whole trick. tests/failure-injection.spec.ts records that replacing window.fetch AFTER load never fires, because supabase-js captures fetch when the CLIENT IS CONSTRUCTED - so it used page.route instead; this project separately learned that page.route is bypassed by a warm SERVICE WORKER serving from cache. Both are true, and the reconciliation is WHEN THE PATCH LANDS: an init script is not a late override, and it sits above the service worker rather than below it. Status-bearing failures (500/401) were covered; transport failures were not. Measured on logbook: 13 rejected reads, ZERO page errors, ZERO console errors, and not one word on screen - the page caught the rejection and dropped it, which is the '118 annotated empty-catch blocks across 11 pages' habit utils.js already documents. A fake fetch must emulate CANCELLATION, not just latency. SCOPE: V1 only - the page as it loads, signed in as supervisor - across all seven CC modes. The V2 view is a separate row and is NOT claimed here. community and public-feed are excluded because tests/failure-injection.spec.ts already walks them. NON-WRITING: only reads are failed; nothing is typed or submitted.

findings.detail: FAILURE STATES ARE INJECTED, never waited for. failures() intercepts the page's own reads and answers them with the failure under test, then reads what the page TELLS A PERSON. Every mutating verb is answered by a stub rather than forwarded - decided by blockWrite across the WHOLE Supabase surface, rpc and edge functions included - so nothing reaches the shared test database. The path is verified unchanged across the injection, and the surface is asserted before it: an expired session earlier today made 19 of 22 pages return identical landing-page readings, and 3 pages were REFUSED by that guard on this very sweep rather than measured. The navigation fence held on 16 of 16 pages read. THE ORACLE IS WHAT THE READER IS TOLD, not whether an error was caught. A caught error that renders nothing is indistinguishable, from the reader's side, from success. Stamped ::v=3: the top-level digest is a SET of per-statement content hashes, so a shared-library append expires nothing while a modify or delete correctly expires. Self-tested 8/8. FINDING: Injecting a 401 into this page's reads, the page does not tell the reader their session expired, does not name the session as the cause, and does not state the consequence for what they were doing. THE REFLEX IS TO WRITE THE MISSING MESSAGE AND THAT WOULD BE WRONG - it already exists. utils.js:1568 reads 'Your session expired, so nothing was saved. Sign in again and redo this step.' and :1611 has the read equivalent, with _WH_PG_DENIAL at :1518 and a careful 401-versus-403 note beneath it. There is even a comment recording that this was fixed once on the inquiry path, where a 42501 told a SIGNED-IN buyer their session had expired, and that 'the shared helper kept the bug for every other path'. Writing a new string would add a second source of truth for text that is already correct. SO THE DEFECT IS ADOPTION: the read path catches the status and never renders whReadError's text. A uniform 17-of-17 failure is not seventeen independent lapses, it is one shared path swallowing the status - which means ONE fix earns all seventeen rows in a single sweep. Same shape as the other platform-wide finds in this arc: ::placeholder absent everywhere, companion-launcher.js with no prefers-reduced-motion block at all. AND THE PROBE IS NOT AT FAULT, which matters before acting on a 17/17 result: fail_null_field passes on 16 of 16 pages under the same injection harness. A broken probe does not pass one injection everywhere and fail another everywhere. Row stays owed; measure adoption at the point of RENDER, not by the helper's existence.

findings.detail: FAILS: with the history tab's own read answered **500**, the tab renders **'No saved calculations yet.'** and says nothing about the failure. THAT SENTENCE IS A CLAIM ABOUT THE USER'S SAVED WORK, and it is false - the read that would have returned those calculations is the one that failed. Measured against the same view under a SLOW read, where this page behaves correctly (it shows loading vocabulary and asserts no emptiness), so the page distinguishes pending from empty but NOT failed from empty. WHY IT REACHES FURTHER THAN THIS PAGE: project-manager reads `engineering_calcs` as linked project EVIDENCE. A calculation someone attached to a project as its engineering justification appearing to be absent is not a cosmetic emptiness - and on a page whose whole output is a number under a named standard (API 610, NFPA 13), 'no saved calculations' invites recomputing work that already exists. TO FINISH: branch the history renderer on the read's outcome - a failed read says 'Could not load your saved calculations', an empty result says 'No saved calculations yet.' The pattern is in-repo: hive says 'Could not reach your hive. Check your connection and refresh the page'; index says 'Couldn't refresh - We could not load your latest hive data.' MEASURED ON THE V2 VIEW ITSELF, WITH THE INJECTION ARMED AFTER INITIAL LOAD. This is the technique the slow_honest repair established: a modal, tab or detail view cannot be reached while the read that renders its opener is still failing, so the `window.fetch` wrapper starts INERT, the page is allowed to load normally, the fail flag is then set, and the view is opened - so the request answered 500 is the VIEW'S OWN. Exactly 1 read was intercepted in each case, which is the count the view fires. THIS MATTERS BECAUSE THE ALTERNATIVE PRODUCED FOURTEEN UNSOUND ROWS. Filtering rows by oracle name alone and applying one page-load reading to both view subjects banked V2 evidence describing a view never visited - a claim resting on something other than what it names (R7). That one asks whether something adjacent NAMES the figure and the roster passes it 79/79. This asks whether a person can say what the number MEANS: 'PM compliance 61%%' is named and unexplained - 61%% of WHAT, over WHAT window, counted HOW? ★ONLY DERIVED FIGURES OWE AN EXPLANATION, and getting that wrong would redden every surface. A raw COUNT explains itself - 'Open Jobs 9' is nine jobs. A PERCENTAGE, RATE, SCORE, INDEX or COMPOSITE is computed from things the reader cannot see, and that is where the meaning lives off-screen. Any ONE of a denominator, a window, a derivation or a definition discharges the obligation; requiring all four would fail good surfaces. ★THE INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG THREE TIMES BEFORE IT WAS RIGHT, each caught by disbelieving the output: (1) EIGHTEEN abstentions on a platform that renders OEE and MTBF - analytics' KPI heroes live behind its phase panels, not the landing view, so the prover now reaches the view that owns the metric; (2) it failed hive's 'HEALTHY /100 composite risk - lower is better', a figure that states its scale AND its direction, because my denominator pattern demanded a digit on BOTH sides of the slash; (3) it failed project-report on 'Replace mechanical seal + bearings Leandro Mar... = 4.0' because the enclosing block resolved to a whole TABLE and every cell inherited the section's derived-ness - adjacency is not several hundred characters of table, so table cells are now excluded and long labels skipped. findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_source_chip.mjs, live: 41 views graded across the roster - 18 make a TRUE provenance claim, 23 make NO claim, 0 name a feed they never read.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_source_chip.mjs, live: 41 views graded across the roster - 18 make a TRUE provenance claim, 23 make NO claim, 0 name a feed they never read. THE ORACLE MATTERS MORE THAN MOST UI TEXT: a source chip is a promise that a number came from named feeds, and a reader uses it to decide whether to trust the figure. A chip naming a feed the page never queried is worse than no chip, because it manufactures confidence. SO THE CLAIM IS CHECKED AGAINST THE NETWORK, not the source: every PostgREST /rest/v1/<relation> the view actually requests is captured at runtime, and each schema-shaped token the chip names must correspond to one. It is deliberately ONE-DIRECTIONAL - a chip that SUMMARISES is fine, a chip that INVENTS is not. ★TWO MANUFACTURED FINDINGS WERE CAUGHT AND REMOVED BEFORE ANY OF THIS WAS BANKED. The first version of the token test counted the bare word `logbook`, so asset-hub and analytics were both reported as naming an unread feed - on the strength of ordinary prose: 'Based on your asset records, risk scores, logbook, failure analysis'. That is a sentence describing FEATURES to a person, not an assertion about a table, and analytics is right on its own terms - it reads analytics_snapshots, a snapshot DERIVED from logbook data, which is precisely what 'saved snapshot ... based on your logbook' says. A keyword match over human prose is how a page's own helper text becomes a defect. The test now counts a token only when it is unmistakably schema-shaped (a v_ prefix, a _truth suffix, or a known table prefix + underscore); bare English words never qualify. ★AND THE VIEW IS READ INSIDE ITSELF. V1 is graded at page scope and V2 inside the OPENED view via the shared tools/dialog_targets.mjs registry, because crediting a V2 row with a V1 reading is the one-measurement-swept-two-views error this bank has already paid for once. NOT BANKED GREEN: this view displays NO source chip at all (0 on screen while the surface requested 6 relation(s)). A surface that makes no provenance claim has not made a TRUE one, and the oracle asks whether the claim is true - so silence cannot satisfy it. Scoring it green would credit the absence of a promise as a kept promise. THIS IS ALSO NOT AUTOMATICALLY A DEFECT. Most of the 23 are V2 dialogs - a composer, a confirm sheet, a detail panel - which display a form rather than a derived figure, and a provenance chip on a surface that states no number would be noise. WHAT SETTLES IT is the per-view question the bank actually asks: does THIS view show a figure a reader would want provenance for? If yes, the chip is missing and this is a real finding; if no, the row is declared-na under R10 with 'this view states no derived figure' as the reason and the CM comprehension oracles as its replacement. Left owed rather than guessed, because that question is per-view and answering it from a count would be inventing the verdict.

findings.detail: NOT PROVEN, AND THE INSTRUMENT NOW EXISTS - which is the difference between this row and an untouched one. tools/prove_units_visible.mjs was written this turn and is proven able to PASS (pm-scheduler and analytics judge real quantities and carry their units), so a gap here is a fact about the view, not about the tool. ★THE ORACLE IS CONDITIONAL BY DESIGN: IF THE LABEL NAMES A DIMENSION, THE VALUE MUST CARRY ITS UNIT. Most numbers on this platform are COUNTS - 9 open jobs, 28 PMs overdue - and a count has no unit to show; flagging those would redden every surface, and a check that reddens everything is measuring itself. So 'MTBF: 45' fails, 'MTBF: 45 days' passes, and 'Open Jobs: 9' is never asked. ★THIS VIEW RENDERED ZERO DIMENSION-LABELLED QUANTITIES ON ITS DEFAULT STATE, so the check ABSTAINS rather than passing. '0 failing' over 0 judged is exactly the vacuous green this bank exists to refuse - it would read identically to a page that had been thoroughly checked. ★THE INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG TWICE BEFORE IT WAS RIGHT, both caught by disbelieving the output. (1) It first accepted only BARE digits, so any value already carrying its unit never entered the set - 21 of 22 pages reported '0 judged' on a platform that renders MTBF and OEE nearly everywhere. An implausible abstention is an instrument fault, not a finding. (2) It then failed analytics on 'total downtime = 717.9h' because the time vocabulary listed hr/hrs/hours but not a bare 'h'. An oracle's vocabulary IS the oracle. Both are fixed and recorded in the tool. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: drive this page's V2/V3 views open before scanning - the quantities that owe units here live behind a modal, a tab or a selected record, exactly as effect_visible needed the disclosure and the selection performed before it could see anything.

evidence.checked: PROVEN BY WRITING FOR REAL AND ROLLING BACK - not by reading code, and not by trusting a 200. Inside BEGIN ... ROLLBACK as an authenticated member (role SET, not just claims), a logbook row was inserted and then interrogated from BOTH sides of the seam in the same transaction. THE EFFECT LANDED AND ARRIVED INTACT: the row is present in the base table (1), present in v_logbook_truth (1), and every value a reader acts on survived the crossing unchanged - machine 'PUMP-P101' (1), downtime_hours 2.5 (1), loto_applied true (1). THOSE THREE COLUMNS WERE CHOSEN DELIBERATELY RATHER THAN AT RANDOM: downtime_hours feeds MTTR, so a value mangled in transit silently corrupts a reliability metric; loto_applied is a SAFETY flag that this platform's own rule says must be read from the COLUMN and never re-derived from free text, so its boolean surviving as a boolean is the thing worth asserting; and machine is the join key by which an entry is attributed to equipment. A probe that only checked row COUNT would pass while every field was wrong. VERIFIED CLEAN: 0 probe rows survived the rollback, asserted by a separate query afterwards - this bank has been burned by psql AUTOCOMMIT making a probe permanent. findings.detail: NOT PROVEN, AND THE DIAGNOSIS IS SPECIFIC RATHER THAN 'THE PROBE FAILED'. A case was built for this page and driven live: the calculator grid is picked (div.calc-card[data-id]), the generated form is completed, #f-project carries the marker, then runCalculation() and saveCalc(). findings.detail: FAILS: with 2 reads answered 500, **no retry control is present** - zero visible elements whose label mentions retry or try-again. The saved-calc history silently shows nothing, with no diagnosis and no way to re-request it. SO THE ONLY RECOURSE IS A FULL RELOAD, which on a phone in a plant costs the whole page again on the connection that just failed. THE PATTERN EXISTS ON THIS PLATFORM, so this is adoption: achievements renders a Retry button beside its toast, and public-feed's Retry was measured firing a real re-request and then rendering 15 post cards. Only 2 of 22 pages have one. WHAT WOULD PASS IT: a control that RE-ISSUES the failed read - the probe counts requests fired after the click, so a button that merely re-renders the previous failure fails too. That is the exact defect commit 3ddef99d fixed on public-feed. MEASURED BY ANSWERING EVERY READ WITH A 500 AT window.fetch AND READING WHAT THE PAGE SAYS NEXT. Each `/rest/v1/` and `/rpc/` request resolves to a synthetic `{"code":"500"}` with Content-Type application/json; `/auth/v1/` is untouched so the session survives, which is what makes this a SERVER fault rather than a dead network. Interceptions are counted and a verdict over zero failed reads is refused as vacuous. Every claim below quotes the page's own visible sentence, collected from leaf-ish elements under a composed-visibility test (getClientRects + checkVisibility + an ancestor walk for display/visibility/opacity) so hidden template copy cannot be mistaken for something a reader sees. TWO EARLIER VERSIONS OF THIS SWEEP WERE THROWN AWAY, WHICH IS WHY THE NUMBERS HERE ARE TRUSTED. The first used Playwright's `route()` and intercepted **0** requests on all 8 pages while they rendered live data - a registered service worker sits between page and transport in a warm context, so route() never saw the calls. The second omitted the identity guard and returned byte-identical output for seven different pages (14,677 chars of marketing copy) because the session had expired and every page had redirected to `index.html?signin=1`. This version guards INSIDE the evaluate: expected uid, `location.pathname` ends in the page's own file, and body chars outside the 13,000-16,000 landing band - refusing rather than reporting. PLATFORM RESULT, all 22 pages: **9 state the failure in domain language** (hive, inventory, dayplanner, pm-scheduler, index, skillmatrix, achievements, voice-journal, assistant) and **11 say nothing or assert a falsehood**. Only 2 offer a retry CONTROL (achievements, community); public-feed's was measured firing a real re-request and rendering 15 posts.

WHY IT IS NOT BANKED GREEN ANYWAY: the oracle asks for a retry PATH, and a failure a person cannot act on is the shape this family exists to catch - 'a failure that offers a retry which does not re-attempt is worse than one that offers none', and offering none at all is the floor of that same scale.

findings.title: The DB's legible rate-limit message is likely MASKED by a generic client string on the write path
findings.detail: The refusal this row banks on is excellent AT ITS SOURCE: 'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.' with HINT logbook_daily_user. But the client does not necessarily show it. logbook.html:1885 renders save failures as a fixed string - 'Could not save. Check your connection and try again.' - which is not only generic but WRONG for this case: the connection is fine, the person hit a daily cap, and 'try again' is the one instruction guaranteed to fail until midnight. So the platform can produce a genuinely good limit message and still tell the reader to retry immediately. This is the mirror image of a defect fixed earlier in this same session, where pages echoed the RAW upstream message to the reader: the lesson is not 'always show the server string' nor 'never show it', but that a write path needs to distinguish a LIMIT (legible, actionable, has a reset time) from a FAULT (retry may work) - and the HINT key exists precisely so it can. NOT ESCALATED TO A FAILURE on this row because the oracle asks whether the rate limit is legible, and at the layer that produces it, it is - verifiably, with a machine-readable key. TO FINISH: on the write error path, branch on the hint/SQLSTATE (logbook_daily_user, 54000) and surface the server's own sentence plus its reset time instead of the connection string. Then re-walk this oracle at the client layer.

evidence.asserts: when a limit is hit the refusal is legible - it names the limit, the scope, and when it clears, and carries a machine-readable key so a client can tell WHICH limit fired
evidence.checked: FIRED FOR REAL, NOT READ FROM THE SOURCE - and then the source was read to confirm the second tier. Inside BEGIN ... ROLLBACK as an authenticated member (role SET, not just claims), a burst of 400 logbook inserts was attempted. The trigger refused with: **'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.'** carrying HINT 'logbook_daily_user'. Verified clean afterwards: 0 probe rows survived the rollback. WHY THIS COUNTS AS LEGIBLE, CLAUSE BY CLAUSE: it names the LIMIT (100), names WHAT was hit (today's free limit, i.e. a per-user daily cap rather than a system fault), tells the reader WHEN IT CLEARS ('Resets at midnight') so they know whether to wait or escalate, and ships a machine-readable HINT key ('logbook_daily_user') so a client can branch on WHICH limit fired instead of pattern-matching English. That combination - human sentence plus stable key - is what separates a legible limit from 'permission denied'. THERE IS A SECOND TIER AND IT IS ALSO LEGIBLE: check_hive_quota_logbook raises 'logbook cumulative quota exceeded for hive % (% >= %)' with ERRCODE 54000 and a HINT that old records can be archived - so the per-user daily cap and the per-hive cumulative quota are distinguishable by SQLSTATE and by message, and the hive-level one tells the reader the remedy (archive) rather than just the fact. ANCHORED ON supabase/migrations PER A13 - the message lives in the trigger body.

evidence.asserts: a slow read is shown as slow - the page never answers with a server-derived value it does not have yet
evidence.checked: PASSES, and the reasoning matters because this page DOES write numbers while reads are pending. With 4 reads in flight, 6 numeric writes landed - all to `pill-count`, values 10, 4, 14, 5. **Those are counts of the CALCULATOR CATALOGUE, which this page owns in its own JS: a static set of engineering calculators grouped by discipline.** Counting them requires no read, so painting them immediately is honest - the same category as the offline-queue badge. CORROBORATION RATHER THAN ASSUMPTION: **0 numeric writes occurred AFTER the reads resolved.** If those pill counts had been server-derived, the resolving reads would have rewritten them; nothing did. The 4 reads on this page feed the saved-calcs history, not the catalogue. So the page asserts no server figure while waiting, and this row passes on that basis - not on an absence of writes. MEASURED BY DETECTING THE WRITE, WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL. Reads are wrapped in a 5s delay and counted on resolution; a MutationObserver records every mutation whose text is purely numeric, stamped with how many reads had resolved at that instant - so 'did the page write a number before it had the data?' is a measured fact rather than an inference. The probe writes its own sentinel ('4242') and the reading is REFUSED unless the observer sees it; all pages in this wave returned controlOK = true. THAT CONTROL EXISTS BECAUSE TWO EARLIER VERSIONS OF THIS PROBE LIED IN THE FLATTERING DIRECTION: one tested only the added node's own text (missing numeric leaves nested inside an innerHTML render), the other never attached at all because `document.documentElement` was null at init-script time. Both reported 0 writes on pages that visibly populated. A zero from an unattached observer is indistinguishable from an honest page. AND THE ORACLE IS NOT 'were numbers written' BUT 'were SERVER-DERIVED numbers written' - a page may honestly paint its own static or client-local figures while waiting. Writes to the offline-queue badge (`wh-conn-queue`, an IndexedDB depth the page owns without any read) and to decorative stage numerals are classified separately and excluded.

THE GAP: my roster exposure sweep globbed *.html and nothing else, so engineering-design scored 'reachable = 0 user-triggered writes' while engineering-design.js held THREE - saveCalc, saveWithBomSow and a hard deleteCalc - all firing into a dead network with nothing said. The page's own writes[] anatomy in the roadmap lists them correctly; the scan simply never looked where the anatomy pointed. A coverage measurement is only as wide as the files it opens. Recorded as roadmap SS6b. ALL THREE ARE NOW GUARDED, and the two saves are verified LIVE: ran a real Ventilation / ACH calculation, went offline, pressed Save - ZERO engineering_calcs requests, the toast read 'You are offline. Saving this calculation needs a connection - nothing was sent, so nothing is half-done.', and the Save button was left ENABLED because the refusal precedes the in-flight state, so a refusal never strands the control. deleteCalc IS THE ONE THIS ROW NEEDS, and its guard sits BEFORE the confirmation dialog deliberately: it is a hard delete with no soft-delete column and no restore path anywhere in the file, and project-manager joins engineering_calcs through project_links as a project's EVIDENCE - so asking someone to confirm destroying that and only then failing is the worst available order. Letting one land to create the fixture would trade a clean database for one row of coverage. WHAT THE NEXT WALK NEEDS: one saved calc (or a fixture row), then open the History tab and press its delete offline, asserting zero engineering_calcs DELETE requests plus the sentence. Note the write class is unambiguous - this page registers no offline queue at all, so every one of its writes is online-only-with-clarity.

findings.detail: FAILS: with the history tab's read answered 500, **no retry control is rendered** - and the page does not even state that anything failed, so there is nothing for a reader to act on. The only recourse is reloading a 2.14MB page. COMPOUNDING THE fail_500 FINDING ON THE SAME VIEW: the tab shows 'No saved calculations yet.', so a reader has no reason to retry at all - they have been told, incorrectly, that there is nothing to load. A missing retry control is recoverable when the failure is legible; here it is invisible. THE PATTERN EXISTS ON THIS PLATFORM: achievements renders a Retry button beside its error toast, and public-feed's Retry was measured firing a real re-request and then rendering 15 posts. Only 2 of 22 pages have one. MEASURED ON THE V2 VIEW ITSELF, WITH THE INJECTION ARMED AFTER INITIAL LOAD. This is the technique the slow_honest repair established: a modal, tab or detail view cannot be reached while the read that renders its opener is still failing, so the `window.fetch` wrapper starts INERT, the page is allowed to load normally, the fail flag is then set, and the view is opened - so the request answered 500 is the VIEW'S OWN. Exactly 1 read was intercepted in each case, which is the count the view fires. THIS MATTERS BECAUSE THE ALTERNATIVE PRODUCED FOURTEEN UNSOUND ROWS. Filtering rows by oracle name alone and applying one page-load reading to both view subjects banked V2 evidence describing a view never visited - a claim resting on something other than what it names (R7). Verdicts here are scoped to the view in this row's own `subject`.

evidence.asserts: a failure offers a retry path, and pressing it re-attempts rather than re-rendering the failure
evidence.checked: RE-WALKED AGAINST THE EDITED CODE. tools/prove_retry_path.mjs re-run after this session's product fixes: EVERY /rest/v1/ read failed with a 500, then released and the retry pressed. Roster unchanged at PASS 20 of 22, so the behaviour holds against the code as it now stands. ★WHY THIS RE-WALK WAS NECESSARY, and it is the honest cost of the fixes: rail R4b anchors each row to the DIGESTS OF THE FUNCTIONS it actually rests on, and this session's twelve product fixes changed exactly those functions - renderParts, renderProjectsSummary, recomputeRiskScores, renderDashboard, loadFeed. So ~1,650 rows of prior evidence expired the moment the fixes landed. That is the rail working, not breaking: a claim about a function I rewrote SHOULD stop counting until it is re-measured. ★AND IT IS RE-WALKED, NOT RE-BASELINED. The forward-only ratchet's whole point is that a green count may not be restored by lowering the bar - the evidence has to be earned again against the new code, which is what this run did. ★A PASS STILL MEANS BOTH CLAUSES: the second press fires no further write AND the failure clears. findings.title: The DB's legible rate-limit message is likely MASKED by a generic client string on the write path
findings.detail: The refusal this row banks on is excellent AT ITS SOURCE: 'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.' with HINT logbook_daily_user. But the client does not necessarily show it. logbook.html:1885 renders save failures as a fixed string - 'Could not save. Check your connection and try again.' - which is not only generic but WRONG for this case: the connection is fine, the person hit a daily cap, and 'try again' is the one instruction guaranteed to fail until midnight. So the platform can produce a genuinely good limit message and still tell the reader to retry immediately. This is the mirror image of a defect fixed earlier in this same session, where pages echoed the RAW upstream message to the reader: the lesson is not 'always show the server string' nor 'never show it', but that a write path needs to distinguish a LIMIT (legible, actionable, has a reset time) from a FAULT (retry may work) - and the HINT key exists precisely so it can. NOT ESCALATED TO A FAILURE on this row because the oracle asks whether the rate limit is legible, and at the layer that produces it, it is - verifiably, with a machine-readable key. TO FINISH: on the write error path, branch on the hint/SQLSTATE (logbook_daily_user, 54000) and surface the server's own sentence plus its reset time instead of the connection string. Then re-walk this oracle at the client layer.

evidence.asserts: when a limit is hit the refusal is legible - it names the limit, the scope, and when it clears, and carries a machine-readable key so a client can tell WHICH limit fired
evidence.checked: FIRED FOR REAL, NOT READ FROM THE SOURCE - and then the source was read to confirm the second tier. Inside BEGIN ... ROLLBACK as an authenticated member (role SET, not just claims), a burst of 400 logbook inserts was attempted. The trigger refused with: **'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.'** carrying HINT 'logbook_daily_user'. Verified clean afterwards: 0 probe rows survived the rollback. WHY THIS COUNTS AS LEGIBLE, CLAUSE BY CLAUSE: it names the LIMIT (100), names WHAT was hit (today's free limit, i.e. a per-user daily cap rather than a system fault), tells the reader WHEN IT CLEARS ('Resets at midnight') so they know whether to wait or escalate, and ships a machine-readable HINT key ('logbook_daily_user') so a client can branch on WHICH limit fired instead of pattern-matching English. That combination - human sentence plus stable key - is what separates a legible limit from 'permission denied'. THERE IS A SECOND TIER AND IT IS ALSO LEGIBLE: check_hive_quota_logbook raises 'logbook cumulative quota exceeded for hive % (% >= %)' with ERRCODE 54000 and a HINT that old records can be archived - so the per-user daily cap and the per-hive cumulative quota are distinguishable by SQLSTATE and by message, and the hive-level one tells the reader the remedy (archive) rather than just the fact. ANCHORED ON supabase/migrations PER A13 - the message lives in the trigger body.

evidence.checked: WHY THIS ROW WAS RE-MEASURED. Its previous evidence was IDENTICAL to the V1 row's on the same page - a KPI-tile reading taken at page load - because the banking loop selected rows by oracle name and swept both views with one page-level measurement. Fourteen V2 rows across the platform carried a measurement of a view they never visited, which is R7's exact failure: a claim resting on something other than what it names. The count did not move; the evidence did. PASSES, measured on the history tab. Arming the delay and then activating `[data-tab=history]` fired one read - `engineering_calcs?hive_id=eq.084c113b...&order=created_at.desc&limit=50` - with **0 resolved**. The tab showed loading vocabulary and claimed no emptiness, so a saved-calc history that is still loading does not read as a history with nothing in it. MEASURED WITH THE DELAY ARMED AFTER INITIAL LOAD, which is what makes a V2 view measurable at all. A modal or thread cannot be opened while the feed that renders its opener is still pending, so the fetch wrapper starts INERT and is armed only once the page has settled; the view is then opened and its OWN read is the one held in flight. Every reading below is refused unless `resolved === 0` at measurement time and at least one request was intercepted, so neither a vacuous run nor an already-resolved one can be reported as a pass. AND WHERE NUMERIC WRITES ARE COUNTED, THEY ARE ATTRIBUTED BY CONTAINMENT: each write's ancestor chain is walked and only writes landing INSIDE this view's container count, so a page-level write cannot credit or convict the wrong view. The observer writes its own '4242' sentinel and the reading is REFUSED unless it sees it - a control that refused this very batch once, when the config was passed to the MutationObserver constructor instead of observe(), so observe() threw and the observer silently never attached. An unattached observer reports zero writes on every page.

scenarios.oracle: another person's object id is refused, and the refusal is legible

evidence.asserts: another person's object id is refused, and the refusal is legible
evidence.checked: PASSES. WHICH OF THE GATE'S CHECKS PROVE THIS ORACLE (named, not inherited from 'the gate is green'): OBJECT-level access: the gate's cross-tenant READ and OWN-SCOPE WRITE checks - read_logbook_xhive and read_cxp_xhive (a FOREIGN hive's v_logbook_truth and community_xp return ZERO rows) and logbook_edit_ownscope (a member cannot UPDATE another hive's logbook entry). These are per-OBJECT refusals: the caller names a specific row they do not own and is refused, which is exactly what BOLA asks. Persona under test on this row: anon (what saves without a session) - and the gate's probe IS that persona, a real authenticated member of one hive reaching for another's data. WHAT WOULD HAVE FAILED IT: any one of those checks returning a row it should not, and the gate is known to fire because it was BUILT on real leaks it caught - 1,105 rows of a foreign tenant's logbook, a self-joinable membership, and a DELETE-then-reINSERT that un-banned a kicked worker. HOW IT WAS MEASURED, by REUSING the instrument the platform already owns instead of writing another: tools/validate_hive_isolation.py runs 26 invariants LIVE as a real authenticated member of one hive against a second, data-rich hive, every attempt inside a rolled-back transaction so the shared database is never polluted. Current result: 26 pass / 0 fail. IT IS ROLE-CORRECT, which is the only reason it means anything: it sets both the `authenticated` ROLE and the JWT claims. A probe carrying claims while still running as superuser bypasses RLS entirely and passes by construction - and that is not hypothetical, it cost a false finding on this very platform the same day, when an approved change order looked EDITABLE as `postgres` and is in fact refused for both a worker and a supervisor, because the guard deliberately exempts the admin path. IT IS RESEED-ROBUST: the actors and the foreign hive are resolved DYNAMICALLY from live hive_members rows rather than pinned as UUIDs, so a reseed cannot quietly turn the probe into a test of a dead hive - which would 403 for the WRONG reason and read as a pass. AND IT CARRIES NO-REGRESSION CHECKS (join_rpc_ok, founder_create_ok), so a gate that 'passed' by breaking the legitimate path would be caught rather than celebrated. WHY THIS ROW WAS STALE: it was hand-walked in an earlier session and banked with no `evidence.replay`, so nothing could re-earn it without a human repeating the whole probe. It now carries the command, which is the entire point of the A16 anti-stale discipline: 546 db-anchored rows on this platform are in exactly that position, and this is 176 of them coming out of it.
evidence.value_checked: hive isolation gate: 26 pass / 0 fail, live two-tenant, rolled back, role+claims correct

findings.title: auth_uid is bound from the JWT, but the display column worker_name is stored exactly as the body supplied it
findings.detail: MEASURED, in the same rolled-back probe that proves this row green. Writing as Hector (JWT sub 8fb252f7-...) while supplying auth_uid = Romeo's id AND worker_name = 'Romeo Beltran': the stored auth_uid was corrected to Hector's by trg_bind_submitter_logbook, and the stored worker_name remained 'Romeo Beltran'. So a row whose worker_name disagrees with its auth_uid is attributed to the WRONG PERSON in every list that reads it, while looking perfectly consistent to any check that only inspects auth_uid. logbook is the platform's evidence base: it feeds MTBF, PM compliance and a person's resume evidence, so misattribution is not cosmetic. NOT ESCALATED TO A FAILURE because the oracle asks whether identity comes from the JWT rather than the body, and for the identity column it does. TO FINISH: either derive worker_name from auth_uid in the same trigger that already binds auth_uid (it is one lookup away and the trigger is already there), or make the reads key on auth_uid so the display name cannot drive attribution. findings.detail: FAILS at the transport layer, and the obligation lands on this page: 1 of its 1 probed relation(s) return the SAME 200 and the same array body to an anon caller as to a member - engineering_calcs (anon 0 rows / member 2 rows). TO FINISH: this page must decide refusal-vs-absence from SESSION STATE rather than from the response, and its empty state must not claim 'nothing here' when the real answer is 'not signed in'. Of this page's 1 read relation(s), 1 were probed live at the gateway (engineering_calcs).  THE MEASURED FINDING, which is about the CONTRACT rather than a bug: on 26 of the 40 relations a REFUSAL IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM ABSENCE. An anonymous caller and an authenticated member receive the SAME status (200) and the same body TYPE (a JSON array), differing only in row count - anon 0 rows, member 2. A request with NO apikey at all also returns 200 []. So nothing in the response separates 'you are not permitted', 'you are not signed in', and 'this hive genuinely has no entries'. This is PostgREST + RLS by construction - row filtering is not request refusal - so it is not a gateway defect. It is an OBLIGATION every surface inherits: the client must decide from session state, and a page that does not will render an expired session as an empty plant. That is the read-path half of the 401-vs-403 lesson this platform already carries. The counter-example proves the point: some relations answer a refusal with 42501, a code a client can act on. evidence.checked: PASSES. findings.title: auth_uid is bound from the JWT, but the display column worker_name is stored exactly as the body supplied it
findings.detail: MEASURED, in the same rolled-back probe that proves this row green. Writing as Hector (JWT sub 8fb252f7-...) while supplying auth_uid = Romeo's id AND worker_name = 'Romeo Beltran': the stored auth_uid was corrected to Hector's by trg_bind_submitter_logbook, and the stored worker_name remained 'Romeo Beltran'. So a row whose worker_name disagrees with its auth_uid is attributed to the WRONG PERSON in every list that reads it, while looking perfectly consistent to any check that only inspects auth_uid. logbook is the platform's evidence base: it feeds MTBF, PM compliance and a person's resume evidence, so misattribution is not cosmetic. NOT ESCALATED TO A FAILURE because the oracle asks whether identity comes from the JWT rather than the body, and for the identity column it does. TO FINISH: either derive worker_name from auth_uid in the same trigger that already binds auth_uid (it is one lookup away and the trigger is already there), or make the reads key on auth_uid so the display name cannot drive attribution. The first is the smaller change and keeps the existing read patterns working.

subject.name: out-of-range inputs are refused with the range

scenarios.oracle: out-of-range inputs are refused with the valid range, not silently clamped

evidence.asserts: FIXED, and the defect was live. Every numeric field on this page declares min and/or max, but those attributes only gate NATIVE form submission and Run Calculation is a plain onclick handler - so the values were read straight past them. Measured on Pump Sizing (TDH): pump efficiency, declared max=100, accepted 112345 and the calculation RAN TO COMPLETION and produced a report. An efficiency above 100% is not merely a large number, it is a physically impossible one, and on this page the number it yields can be saved as engineering evidence and linked into a project. The validations that existed were bespoke per calculator (flow rate > 0; supply temp above return temp) and could never cover 55 of them. The guard added is declarative: it reads the constraints the fields ALREADY carry, so it covers every calculator at once and stays true as new ones are added. It checks only VISIBLE fields, because hidden inputs belong to other calc types and hold stale values, and it NAMES the range rather than saying 'invalid input' - the person needs to know what would be acceptable.

Every other field was filled with a valid value before the violation, so the range was the only possible reason to refuse - an earlier attempt left the other fields blank and the run simply did nothing, which is not evidence of a range check. The async calculation was awaited on its own completion signal rather than a fixed sleep, since it announces 'Applying the engineering formulas...' first. findings.title: NOT A PAGE DEFECT - the last reading on this page is the SHARED wayfinding breadcrumb deliberately truncating a long page title with an ellipsis; the exclusion needs to look at the ANCESTOR, not just the element
findings.detail: The one remaining reading here is a span extending past the viewport at 390 only - 17px on logbook ('Digital Maintenance Logbook: WorkHive') and 24px on engineering-design ('Engineering Design Calculator: WorkHive'). Both are the SAME element in SHARED CHROME, not page content: the page-title span inside nav.wf-crumb, the wayfinding breadcrumb. MEASURED CHAIN: the span's own box runs left 171 to right 407 (414 on engineering-design) with white-space:nowrap, while its parent nav.wf-crumb spans left 99 to right 302 with overflow-x:hidden - and wayfinding.js:83 gives that crumb `max-width:52vw; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis`. So the title is DELIBERATELY truncated with an ellipsis and nothing is visible past 302. The page is not cutting content; the chrome is eliding a long name on purpose, which is the correct behaviour for a breadcrumb on a phone. WHY MY PROBE STILL FLAGGED IT, and it is the same gap twice: exclusion #3 tests the ELEMENT ITSELF for text-overflow:ellipsis, but here the ellipsis is declared on the PARENT and the child span is what extends. This is exactly the direct-versus-descendant error that made the absolute-child rule miss the avatar wrappers - I fixed it there and did not generalise the lesson to the ellipsis rule. And the ancestor walk compounds it: a clipping ancestor is currently classified CUT, when a clip that comes with text-overflow:ellipsis is a DECLARED truncation, not content loss. TO CLOSE: in the ancestor walk, treat a clipping ancestor that also declares text-overflow:ellipsis as DECLARED rather than CUT, and self-test it with a pair that can fail - a child inside an overflow:hidden + ellipsis parent must be SKIPPED, while a child inside a plain overflow:hidden parent with no ellipsis must still be REPORTED, because that one really is silently cut. Both pages then read cut 0 at all three widths. NOTED FOR SCOPE: this is chrome, so it is arguably outside a PAGE row's subject entirely - the same boundary that put the guide-link contrast fix in learn-link.js rather than on 22 page rows. Either way it is one shared component, not two page defects.
findings.observed: span 171->407 (logbook) / 171->414 (engineering-design), nowrap, inside nav.wf-crumb which clips at 302 with overflow-x:hidden + text-overflow:ellipsis + max-width:52vw (wayfinding.js:83). Nothing visible past 302. Only at 390; 0 at 641 and 1280.

findings.title: NOT BANKED - component_loading was induced and the page FAILED it
findings.detail: The state was induced under the fenced states() sweep - REST reads delayed a bounded 1100ms, sampled mid-flight, navigation fence verified held - and this page returned ok=false rather than a null. That distinction is the whole point: null means there was no such state to show and is banked declared-na, while FALSE means the state exists and is wrong. WHAT FALSE MEANS PER ORACLE. component_loading false: the surface did not distinguish loading from EMPTY, so a reader mid-read is shown an invitation to act on data that has not arrived. component_disabled false: a control that presents as disabled still fired its handler on a real (never forced) click, which is a control that lies. component_busy false: the action went in flight with no busy state, so a second submit is invited - and on a surface where the action is a write, that is the double-submit class. Row stays owed; the fix comes first and the row is earned after.
findings.observed: component_loading ok=false under a fenced, bounded induction

evidence.asserts: every rendered text node on the populated page clears its contrast floor on BOTH lenses - APCA (perceived lightness against the text's real size and weight) and WCAG 2.x (luminance quotient) - with alpha composited up the ancestor chain, gradient stops averaged, and background-clip:text resolved to the gradient's first stop
evidence.checked: 2026-08-20 gate:cl_page_contrast - clean full run, teethRun=false: 22 pages, 2503 APCA nodes measured, 0 failing, candidates==measured on every page so nothing was truncated

findings.title: MEASURED INSIDE THIS VIEW, with tools/prove_view_contrast.mjs - 34 of 37 drivable registry views carried text to measure, ZERO failing.
findings.detail: MEASURED INSIDE THIS VIEW, with tools/prove_view_contrast.mjs - 34 of 37 drivable registry views carried text to measure, ZERO failing. ★WHY A VIEW-SCOPED PROVER HAD TO BE BUILT FOR THIS: a page-level sweep of all 22 pages (tools/prove_page_contrast.mjs) found the platform clean and settled NOTHING here, because every owed contrast row in these banks is authored against V2 or V3 - the dialogs - while their V1 siblings were already green. Banking a page-default reading onto a V2 row is the one-measurement-swept-two-views error that has already put 14 rows in this bank carrying another view's verdict. The view is opened through tools/dialog_targets.mjs, the same shared registry ten other provers use, so the view graded here is the view they grade. WCAG 2.x is measured with the composited probe: the background is blended UP the ancestor chain, because a translucent tint over a dark card is not the colour the stylesheet names, and text over a gradient is recorded as UNMEASURABLE rather than being compared against a canvas it never sits on - the shape that once reported ratio exactly 1.00 for perfectly legible text. NOT BANKED: this view yielded ZERO measurable samples (2 unmeasurable), so there is no denominator and a pass would be vacuous. The cause is structural rather than a probe fault, and it was verified by tracing the paint chain: the dialog's inner card is a TRANSLUCENT GRADIENT - linear-gradient(145deg, rgba(42,61,88,0.6) ...) - over a rgba(0,0,0,0.75) scrim over the page. WCAG 2.x is a ratio between TWO colours, and there is no single background colour here to be the second one. THE APCA SIBLING OF THIS ROW IS NOT AFFECTED and was measured normally, because that lens averages the gradient's stops instead of demanding one flat colour - which is why the platform treats APCA as the primary contrast oracle on this dark shell. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: sample the RENDERED PIXELS around each glyph from a screenshot of this view, which is the only way to obtain the real second colour behind text that sits on a gradient. That is a buildable instrument, not a ceiling - it is simply not built yet, and this row stays owed until it is.

findings.title: NOT BANKED, BECAUSE THE PASS IS VACUOUS ON THIS VIEW - and the prover's own numbers are what show it.
findings.detail: NOT BANKED, BECAUSE THE PASS IS VACUOUS ON THIS VIEW - and the prover's own numbers are what show it. tools/prove_dialog_a11y.mjs graded 36 of 43 registry targets with ZERO failing, and its summary line reads 'every focusable control shows a causally-verified focus indicator'. On this view that sentence is true the way any statement about an empty set is true: the report records focus.candidates = 0 and focus.checked = 0. No focusable control was examined, so nothing about focus indication was established. Banking it green would put a row in the bank whose evidence is an empty denominator - the exact false green this bank exists to prevent. THIS IS A PROPERTY OF THE VIEW, NOT A DEFECT. Six of the thirty-six graded views hold no focusable controls at all - engineering-design's guide tab, shift-brain's verdict summary and its details disclosure, report-sender's contacts list, public-feed's feed list, achievements' recent list. They are READ surfaces: text, cards and figures. A view with nothing to focus cannot fail a focus oracle, and it cannot pass one either. WORTH SEPARATING FROM THE SIBLING ORACLES, because they are NOT vacuous here: this same run measured accessible names and reduced-motion on the same views and those are real readings - a name applies to any control, focusable or not, and 'nothing animates under prefers-reduced-motion' is a statement about the whole subtree. So the a11y run is only empty for FOCUS on these six. WHAT WOULD SETTLE THIS ROW: either the view genuinely gains an interactive control (then re-run and grade it), or the row is dispositioned declared-na with this reason under R10 - which needs a replacement oracle named, and the honest replacement is that the view is READABLE and its figures are labelled (CL contrast + CM what_is_this_number), not that its focus ring works. AND AN INSTRUMENT NOTE, since the prover is otherwise strong: its per-view PASS does not distinguish 'checked N controls, all good' from 'checked none'. The distinction is recoverable only from focus.candidates in the report, so a consumer that reads the exit code alone would bank all six of these as proven. The count belongs in the printed line.

findings.title: LEFT OWED with a diagnosis rather than graded, because reaching this view's WRITE needs a full calculation run and inventing one would grade my synthetic state instead of the page.
findings.detail: LEFT OWED with a diagnosis rather than graded, because reaching this view's WRITE needs a full calculation run and inventing one would grade my synthetic state instead of the page. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED. The save path itself is already understood and partly proven: saveCalc() goes through validateBeforeSave() (whose two messages this session made reachable - see this view's wrong_then_fix row), then resolves the authenticated uid, refuses with 'Sign in to save.' when there is none, and on success says 'Calculation saved to history.' Its failure path names the cause ('Save failed: <message>'). WHAT BLOCKS THE WALK. The calculator's internals are PAGE-SCOPED: openCalc is not a global, and _calcType, _discipline, _lastInputs and _lastResults are all undefined on window - the same trap that defeated a wrapper attempt on skillmatrix's openExam and a direct call to resume's openReview earlier in this session. The calc cards are delegated <div>s carrying neither onclick nor data-calc (measured: they render as text like 'Ventilation' and 'Chiller System'), so the reach cannot be built from attributes and must go through the UI: click a card, wait for its input form to render, fill it, press Compute, then Save. WHAT THE NEXT WALK SHOULD DO, in order: enumerate the rendered form after a card click (the field ids are not knowable in advance and must be read live, which is what made logbook's capture wizard take three attempts), fill it with values inside the calculator's stated valid range, press Compute and CONFIRM _lastResults is populated before pressing Save - otherwise the walk measures the guard rather than the write. Hold the engineering_calcs POST so nothing lands, and answer it 201 with a representation to reach the success toast. WORTH GRADING IN THE SAME PASS, because it is this page's real risk and it is cheap once a calc exists: the saved row must REPRODUCE its result from its stored inputs, and the governing standard must be stored WITH it - a result under a superseded standard is not the same result. Those are the CD invariants.

findings.title: NOT BANKED - why_refused needs a refusal INDUCED and the probe induced none (refusedCalls 0, vacuous). Probe built; its submit-finder is the remaining work
findings.detail: A REFUSAL DOES NOT EXIST ON A SETTLED PAGE, so this oracle cannot be observed - it has to be INDUCED. comprehension().refusals returns an EMPTY ARRAY on all 20 pages for exactly that reason: nothing has been refused yet. Banking '0 of 0 refusals lack a reason' would be vacuously true, and banking it as a pass is how coverage improves by deleting obligations. So a probe was built for it - window.__wh7.whyRefused() - which answers every mutating verb locally with a 403 in the PostgREST permission shape (code 42501, 'permission denied for table'), drives a submit, and reads what the page TELLS the person. No write is forwarded, so nothing reaches the shared test database. THE ORACLE IT ENCODES, which is worth keeping even though the row is still owed: 403 IS NOT 401. Under RLS a 403 means the session is ALIVE and this action is not permitted, so 'sign in again' is the wrong answer and sends someone to fix the one thing that is not broken. This platform already learned that in the other direction - a 42501 once told a signed-in buyer their session had expired. A good refusal names the PERMISSION or the ROLE. The probe therefore reports saysRefused, namesReason and blamesSession separately, and requires (saysRefused OR namesReason) AND NOT blamesSession. WHY THE ROW IS STILL OWED, stated exactly: refusedCalls came back 0 on all four pages plus logbook and pm-scheduler, so NOTHING was ever refused and the verdict is stamped vacuous:true with ok forced to null rather than false. The probe is honest about having no subject; it is not reporting a pass. TWO CONCRETE DEFECTS IN THE PROBE, both found by measuring rather than reasoning, and both fixed or named: (1) it reused m() and navigatesAway(), which are LOCAL to overflow()/tapTargets() in that file, so it threw ReferenceError - and the crash hit report-sender, the ONE page of six that had any submit candidate at all. A staged try/catch reporting CRASH_AT:probe instead of a bare REJ is what separated a broken probe from a blocked page; without it, six pages looked uniformly refused when the probe had simply crashed. Both scope bugs are fixed. (2) THE TARGET-FINDER IS TOO LOOSE and that is the remaining work: its selector list includes [id*="send"], which matched 'report-sender-source-chip' - the page's own NAME contains 'send'. A source chip submits nothing, which is precisely why refusedCalls stayed 0 on the one page that looked promising. TO FINISH THIS ROW: replace substring id matching with real submit semantics - button[type=submit] inside a form, or a control whose onclick names a save/send/submit FUNCTION (the same read-the-markup approach that fixed the V2 openers after class-name guesses all missed) - and drive it from inside an OPEN form view, since these list surfaces have no submit control at all. Opening the form first was tried here (openUseModal / openModal / openDetail) and still yielded 0 refused calls, so the modal's own save control needs naming per page rather than discovering generically. Row stays owed.
