evidence.checked: LIVE MCP BROWSER walk, 2026-08-06, /workhive/engineering-design.html at 853 physical px (innerWidth 1280), signed in as Pablo Aguilar. Landing-page guard applied (char count asserted not 14449/14551). REACHING THE SUBJECT TOOK A 4-STEP INDUCTION and two of my own probe errors, recorded so they are not repeated: the calculator is a wizard, and its inputs do not exist until a calc TYPE is chosen. A search for onclick handlers named selectCalc/loadCalc found NOTHING because the calculation cards are DIVs bound via addEventListener - invisible to an [onclick] attribute scan; they were located via computed cursor:pointer plus their container #calc-type-grid > .calc-card. An earlier attempt to 'fill the inputs' at rest found only #wh-fb-subject, which belongs to the shared FEEDBACK widget, not the calculator. The working path is selectDiscipline('Mechanical') -> click the .calc-card '💧 Pump Sizing (TDH)' -> 12 calculator fields render (f-flow-rate, f-static-head, f-pipe-length, f-pipe-dia, f-suction-head, f-pressure-head, f-pump-eff, f-motor-eff, f-fittings, f-fluid-density, f-project, calc-search) with 7 pre-filled defaults and 5 empty. THE REFUSAL WAS DRIVEN, and it is a good one. With the 5 empty fields left empty, #calc-btn 'Run Calculation' is ENABLED - and clicking it refuses the calculation with the toast 'Please enter the flow rate.' No report is produced: the result pane still reads 'No Report Yet' and the page stays at 1764 characters. WHY THAT MESSAGE IS RIGHT RATHER THAN MERELY PRESENT: it names the SPECIFIC missing field (the flow rate) rather than a generic 'fill in all fields', so the way out is unambiguous among twelve inputs - and f-flow-rate is genuinely the first empty one that the calculation needs. A generic message would have left a person hunting. AND IT REACHES ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGY, which is the half that usually fails: the same text was captured from BOTH a toast element AND a [role=alert] node, so it is announced rather than only painted. That is the difference from the defect I fixed on logbook earlier today, where the step-1 refusal was a pure colour flash with no text and no aria at all. THE HAPPY PATH WAS DRIVEN TOO, so the refusal is proven to be conditional rather than a dead button: filling all 5 remaining fields with values inside their own declared ranges (each field carries min/max - f-pump-eff 1-100, f-fittings 0-100 - so the values used were in-range, not arbitrary) and clicking again produced 'Calculation complete!', took the page from 1764 to 5198 characters, and rendered a real Total Dynamic Head result. That is a legitimate design choice - it lets the message name the missing field, which a disabled button cannot do - and it is the reason this page's component_disabled row rests on the calc-not-yet-selected state instead. Whether a disabled state would serve better is a design question, not this oracle's. NOTHING WAS WRITTEN: a run is a pure client-side computation on this page; only an explicit Save writes engineering_calcs, and Save was never clicked. Zero /rest/v1 and /functions/v1 requests fired across the whole calculation.

evidence.checked: PASSES: redirected to "index" — the expected auth wall for an anon persona on a private page, and it offers 65 actionable control(s). No claim is made about engineering-design's own content, which this persona never sees.. PERSONA: this row was walked as "anon (the free public tools)" (slot P1), the label this page's own anatomy names, established as identity 'anon'. HOW THE JOURNEY WAS CONSTRUCTED. Each row is walked live in a throwaway browser context as the persona the page's OWN anatomy names: page_bank_anatomy/<page>.json `journey_personas` supplies the label (e.g. 'worker (own entries)', 'two_context (two techs, one PM)'), and the harness maps it to an identity it can actually establish - supervisor and worker are real signed-in accounts, anon and crawler get no session, two_context opens BOTH accounts concurrently on the same page. A label that maps to no identity is FAILED, never defaulted to a signed-in worker and never skipped: defaulting is exactly how a persona claim gets banked for the wrong identity. FIRST RUN means everything a returning visitor would CARRY is removed, while everything that constitutes their IDENTITY is preserved: localStorage and sessionStorage are cleared apart from the sb-*/supabase auth keys, the hive-membership keys (wh_active_hive_id / wh_hive_id / wh_hive_role / wh_hive_name) and the worker-name keys (wh_last_worker / wh_worker_name / workerName). Wiping auth would test the sign-in wall instead of the journey; wiping the other two would test a DIFFERENT person entirely. findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing. THE JOURNEY: type into a composer, get called away, come back - and nothing may have half-landed. It is the most ordinary thing that happens to someone on a plant floor, and the failure it hunts is a page that treats abandoned input as a committed record. ★THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES THE VERDICT FAIR, and without which this oracle would punish good behaviour: after the reload the marker text is looked for in TWO places, and they mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD means a DRAFT was deliberately preserved - that is good UX and passes. Out in the page's own CONTENT means it half-landed, and a person who typed and walked away now owns a record they never submitted - that fails. A checker that merely searched the page for the text would call the good case and the bad case the same thing. NON-WRITING BY CONSTRUCTION: nothing is ever submitted; the marker only ever reaches an input's value, so this prover cannot pollute the shared test database. The composer inventory comes from tools/dialog_targets.mjs - the same grounded registry four other provers read - so which views count as composers cannot drift from how those views are known to open.FOR THIS PAGE AND PERSONA THERE IS NOTHING TO ABANDON. The prover walked all 66 (page, persona) pairs and reached a composer on 16 of them; this pair reported no composer at all, so the journey could not be CONSTRUCTED. ★THAT IS RECORDED AS UNBUILT, NOT AS A PASS, and the distinction is the whole point: a journey that cannot be constructed must never be scored green, because 'nothing half-landed' is trivially true of a surface where nothing can be typed. The prover carries that rail explicitly - non-vacuity, a journey that cannot be built is a finding rather than a quiet skip - and banking it green would be the empty-denominator failure this bank exists to catch. WHY THIS PAIR HAS NONE: the composer inventory is tools/dialog_targets.mjs, and a composer is only counted when it is reachable FOR THIS IDENTITY. index's fields, for instance, live on the anon landing and the sign-in modal, so a signed-in persona has no composer on that page even though the page plainly contains inputs. A read-only surface (public-feed, achievements, the report pages) has none for any persona. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: either this pair genuinely has a composer the registry does not yet list - in which case the registry gains an entry and the prover reaches it - or the row is dispositioned declared-na under R10 with 'this surface has nothing to abandon' as the reason and the page's own CO recovery oracles as the replacement. Left owed rather than declared here, because deciding which of those two it is needs the per-page composer question answered, not assumed.

evidence.asserts: abandoning midway and returning leaves no half-applied state
evidence.checked: MEASURED with tools/prove_abandon_resume.mjs - 13 capture surfaces across the roster opened, filled with a marker only this run could produce, then ABANDONED BY RELOAD. 13 of 13 pass: zero rows written, zero silent drafts, every cleanup verified. ★ABANDONMENT IS A RELOAD, NOT A CLOSE. An X is CANCELLING, which pages handle deliberately; a reload is what happens when someone takes a call or their phone dies, and no confirm dialog can intercept it. ★THREE SHAPES, judged separately: a ROW THAT SHOULD NOT EXIST; a DRAFT THAT DOES NOT SAY IT IS A DRAFT (a restored draft is the GOOD design - judged on the LABEL, never on the restoration); and a QUEUED WRITE draining later. And the MEASURE FOLLOWS THE SHAPE OF THE WRITE: hive's intent capture mutates a row, so that case compares the VALUE before and after rather than counting rows, which a count-delta could never detect. ★EVERY GREEN IS NON-VACUOUS - the fill is proven to have landed first. Three cases failed LOUDLY on the way in rather than passing quietly: logbook on an invented opener (UNGRADED), pm-scheduler on a guessed column name (task_text; it is item_text), resume on a JSONB column needing ::text. A PROBE WHOSE OWN QUERY IS BROKEN MUST NOT REPORT A FINDING, because its 0 rows look exactly like a page that wrote nothing.  FOR THIS PAGE: the form does not exist until a CALCULATOR IS CHOSEN - this is a grid of cards and picking one renders that calc's inputs, so a probe that fills before choosing fills nothing. Chosen, filled, abandoned: no row in engineering_calcs, nothing pre-filled.

findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing. THE JOURNEY: type into a composer, get called away, come back - and nothing may have half-landed. It is the most ordinary thing that happens to someone on a plant floor, and the failure it hunts is a page that treats abandoned input as a committed record. ★THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES THE VERDICT FAIR, and without which this oracle would punish good behaviour: after the reload the marker text is looked for in TWO places, and they mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD means a DRAFT was deliberately preserved - that is good UX and passes. Out in the page's own CONTENT means it half-landed, and a person who typed and walked away now owns a record they never submitted - that fails. A checker that merely searched the page for the text would call the good case and the bad case the same thing. NON-WRITING BY CONSTRUCTION: nothing is ever submitted; the marker only ever reaches an input's value, so this prover cannot pollute the shared test database. The composer inventory comes from tools/dialog_targets.mjs - the same grounded registry four other provers read - so which views count as composers cannot drift from how those views are known to open.FOR THIS PAGE AND PERSONA THERE IS NOTHING TO ABANDON. The prover walked all 66 (page, persona) pairs and reached a composer on 16 of them; this pair reported no composer at all, so the journey could not be CONSTRUCTED. ★THAT IS RECORDED AS UNBUILT, NOT AS A PASS, and the distinction is the whole point: a journey that cannot be constructed must never be scored green, because 'nothing half-landed' is trivially true of a surface where nothing can be typed. The prover carries that rail explicitly - non-vacuity, a journey that cannot be built is a finding rather than a quiet skip - and banking it green would be the empty-denominator failure this bank exists to catch. WHY THIS PAIR HAS NONE: the composer inventory is tools/dialog_targets.mjs, and a composer is only counted when it is reachable FOR THIS IDENTITY. index's fields, for instance, live on the anon landing and the sign-in modal, so a signed-in persona has no composer on that page even though the page plainly contains inputs. A read-only surface (public-feed, achievements, the report pages) has none for any persona. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: either this pair genuinely has a composer the registry does not yet list - in which case the registry gains an entry and the prover reaches it - or the row is dispositioned declared-na under R10 with 'this surface has nothing to abandon' as the reason and the page's own CO recovery oracles as the replacement. Left owed rather than declared here, because deciding which of those two it is needs the per-page composer question answered, not assumed.

evidence.asserts: a second press on Delete cannot destroy two records
evidence.checked: LIVE WALK with every DELETE held and counted. Pressed a row's Delete TWICE: zero delete requests - the confirm gate absorbs both presses. Confirming once then fired exactly one delete. MEASURED WITH EVERY DELETE HELD, so the gate could be tested without destroying a saved calculation: pressing a row's Delete opened the confirm dialog ('Delete this calculation?' / Cancel / Delete) and fired ZERO delete requests; Cancel dismissed it, still zero; press-then-confirm fired exactly ONE. ONE WART, NOW CLOSED: the second press STACKS a second confirm dialog (two live dialogs measured), and cancelling leaves the first still open. Nothing is destroyed and no write escapes, so this row passes on its own terms - but a person who double-taps has to dismiss twice, and that is worth a fix on the dialog layer rather than here. ★THIS VIEW WAS ABOUT TO BE DISPOSITIONED AS HAVING NOTHING TO COMMIT, and that would have thrown away the most consequential control on the page. My commit detector's verb list was entirely ADDITIVE - save, send, add, submit, publish - so the History pane enumerated as 'nothing editable, nothing to commit' while carrying five red Delete buttons wired to deleteCalc() -> engineering_calcs.delete(). A destructive control is exactly where a double-tap and a mis-tap cost something, so the omission was worst precisely where it mattered. The detector now recognises delete, remove, discard, clear, archive, revoke, cancel, unpublish and reset, and the same pane immediately reported five commit controls. ★AND THE CONFIRMATION DID NOT SAY IT WAS PERMANENT. The shipped copy was 'Deleted.' This is a HARD delete - db.from('engineering_calcs').delete(), auth_uid-scoped, with no soft-delete column and no restore path anywhere in the file - so it now reads 'Deleted -> removed from your saved calculations. This cannot be undone.', verified live off the surface after a synthetic 204. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED, because the code does not keep the promise: whether anything LINKED to the calc is affected. project-manager joins engineering_calcs through project_links, so a deleted calc can become a project's missing evidence, and nothing in this path checks for that. This page's own CD invariant already names it - 'deleting a calc a project links to does not silently break the project's evidence' - and it is still owed. Saying 'nothing else is affected' would have been the easy sentence and a false one. ★AND THE STACKED-DIALOG WART IS NOW FIXED, in the shared builder rather than on this page. Both destructive controls audited this session (this one and its counterpart on the other page) stacked a SECOND confirm dialog on a second press, and cancelling dismissed only the top one - leaving an identical question waiting behind it. Nothing was ever written, which is why these rows passed on their own terms, but on a destructive control an extra dialog is exactly where a person clicks through on autopilot. Because both cases came from ONE builder (utils.js _mount, behind whConfirm/whPrompt), the fix belongs there: while a confirm is open a second request now resolves FALSE - the safe answer, since false can only decline an action, never perform one - instead of opening a rival dialog. The gate is released in dispose() FIRST and unconditionally, because a guard that fails to release would be worse than the wart it replaces: every later confirm on the page would silently resolve false and destructive controls would appear dead. RE-MEASURED ON BOTH PAGES: a second press now yields ONE dialog (was two), Cancel leaves ZERO (was one stranded), and press-then-confirm still fires exactly one write - so the gate releases.
